It’s a game-changer for both companies and the software world at large. ## Why Bending Spoons? Why Now? Bending Spoons, fresh off its July 2026 public debut at an $18 billion valuation, is on a mission. It’s no stranger to big acquisitions, having added Evernote, WeTransfer, EventBrite, and Vimeo to its portfolio. But this marks its first acquisition since going public. hits.snippet: The most valuable no-code company of the last decade just changed hands for a number that would have been unthinkable five years ago. On August 4, 2026, Bending Spoons agreed to acquire Airtable for US$1.285 billion in an all-cash deal, a staggering drop from the US$11.7 billion valuation Airtable commanded at the peak of the 2021 software boom. For anyone tracking where enterprise software is heading, this is not just a headline about one company. It is a signal about how the ground has shifted under the entire SaaS industry. Bending Spoons paid an enterprise value of US$1.285 billion, with an implied equity value closer to US$2.25 billion once Airtable's net cash is included. Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons' CEO, called Airtable "a pioneering brand reshaping how teams organize data and manage critical workflows." Airtable co-founder and CEO Howie Liu noted that "more than 500,000 organizations rely on Airtable to power their most critical work." ## Who is Bending Spoons If the buyer's name is unfamiliar, the apps it owns are not.
